question.text: Under SEBI regulations, what is the validity period of the NISM Series V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification, and what is required for renewal?

answer.text: 3 years validity; renewal through CPE (Continuing Professional Education) or re-examination before expiry
5 years validity; no renewal required — lifetime certification
1 year validity; annual re-examination is mandatory
10 years validity; renewal through a simple online test

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification, like other NISM mandatory certifications, carries a validity of three years from the date of passing the exam. To remain ARN-active beyond that period, a distributor must either pass a Continuing Professional Education (CPE) programme conducted by an approved provider before the certificate's expiry or re-take and clear the NISM Series V-A examination. Allowing the certificate to lapse without renewal results in suspension of the ARN until a fresh certification is obtained. The Trap: A 5-year lifetime certification, an annual re-examination, and a 10-year validity with a "simple online test" are not consistent with NISM's standard certification framework. NISM mandatory certifications are designed to be refreshed every three years, with CPE as the principal mechanism for renewal. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.4, p.6, p.80, p.120-p.122) discuss NISM certification, CPE programmes, KYD, ARN and empanelment but do not explicitly state the 3-year validity and the CPE / re-examination renewal rule. The framing above is drawn from the general NISM / SEBI certification framework as widely applied to mutual fund distributors.
